paragraphs: Mentioned in [Shabbat 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.60a.9-12). The Gemara first gives Shmuel's statement, then his, followed by Rami bar Yechezkel's. Hyman infers from this arrangement that he was one of Shmuel's students.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The sequence of speakers is Hyman’s reason for inferring discipleship, rather than a direct statement that the Talmud names a teacher.

Shmuel, Rabbi Ilai ben Elazar, and Rami bar Yechezkel give different accounts of the decree on the spiked sandal. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=491&lang=en) records the forms Eliezer and Elisha and puts Ilai in Shmuel’s time. The inference of discipleship is Hyman’s.
